payload.name: Extract explicit praise as preference during planning
payload.description: When a speaker explicitly praises an attribute of a place, activity, or plan during conversation, use it as preference evidence and extract a memory.
content: During candidate extraction, treat explicit positive evaluative statements (e.g., 'X is beautiful', 'I love Y', 'Z looks awesome') as preference signals for the speaker, even when they appear inside a suggestion, question, or plan. Create a preference candidate linking the speaker to the praised object or attribute. Do not skip such utterances because the main clause is about planning.

candidates.solves: During construction-stage extraction from multi-turn planning conversations, the agent sometimes fails to create a memory when an explicit positive appraisal is embedded in a suggestion or plan. This rule makes any clear evaluative praise of a place, activity, or attribute trigger preference extraction, independent of the topic. It applies whenever a speaker says something is beautiful, great, awesome, or similar while discussing future plans.

payload.name: Extract explicit self-disclosed strategies and reasons
payload.description: When a speaker directly states how they stay confident, motivated, or handle challenges, or gives reasons for their own actions, extract these as durable profile or preference memories during candidate extraction.
content: During extraction, treat explicit first-person statements about the speaker's own stable strategies, habits, sources of support, or reasons for starting or continuing an endeavor as durable memory candidates.
Create one compact profile or preference memory per distinct strategy or reason, with the speaker as subject and a source link to the message.
Do not require the statement to be a response to a direct question; advice or reflective statements also carry extractable facts about the speaker.

candidates.solves: Diagnosed cause: a message explicitly containing Gina's confidence-maintenance strategies was processed but produced no candidates, so the facts were never stored. The reusable mechanism is missing extraction of explicit self-disclosed stable strategies and reasons. Future conversations where a user states their own methods, habits, sources of support, or reasons for starting/continuing an endeavor should trigger extraction, regardless of topic; it does not apply to extracting traits of third parties or one-off transient statements.

payload.name: Extract Explicit Personal Preference Statements
payload.description: When a message contains an explicit statement of a person's favorite, liked, disliked, or preferred item/activity, extract a preference memory during candidate extraction.
content: During extraction, when any speaker explicitly states a personal preference, favorite, like, dislike, or attribute (e.g., 'my favorite X is Y', 'I love/like/dislike X', 'I prefer Y', 'I am/have ...'), create a candidate memory using the appropriate type (preference, profile, or state).
Do not skip extraction merely because the statement is part of a longer turn, is conversational, or is not the main question; directly stated personal facts are always memory-worthy.

candidates.solves: The diagnosed cause was that the construction agent processed a message containing an explicit statement of a favorite dish but produced no candidate memory, so the fact was never stored. The abstract failure mechanism is missing extraction of directly stated personal preferences/attributes from any speaker. A rule to always extract such explicit statements is supported because these are durable, evidence-bound facts that future questions about the person require, and it applies to any conversation where a participant states a favorite, preference, or personal attribute.
